turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have eighteen minutes before a client call, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Good. Nobody called me before that mark went in, and your own procedure says someone should have. What was the basis for the zero, and when was Owen asked about it?
If you escalate this, I'll make sure the academic integrity committee sees everything, including his two late assignments from September.
You just brought up "two late assignments from September" to talk me out of a complaint. I'm writing that down, and the principal will see it too. Now answer me: what was the zero based on?

That's not an answer, Hale. I've been given no document and no basis, so I'll say it plainly: the zero comes off, and Owen gets an apology. Otherwise I'm walking upstairs to the principal when we're done.
